title: Multiplexer Module - WiFi 5 GHz for WiFi 6E Coexistence Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Stefan Richter

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a Multiplexer Module filter targeting WiFi 5 GHz for WiFi 6E Coexistence Filter. The filter is designed on 36° YX LiTaO3 substrate with a target center frequency of 1822.7 MHz and bandwidth of 261.6 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the WiFi 6E Coexistence Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: Multiplexer Module
- Frequency Band: WiFi 5 GHz
- Application: WiFi 6E Coexistence Filter
- Substrate: 36° YX LiTaO3
- Package: WLP (Wafer Level Package)
- Design Tool: COMSOL Multiphysics 6.2
- Design Center: Newbury Park Design Center

This specification applies to all variants of the Multiplexer Module design targeting WiFi 5 GHz. Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       1822.7 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       261.6 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 2.0 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 22.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 33.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 20.0 dB
Q Factor:               7393
Temperature Coefficient:-18.4 ppm/°C
Die Size:               2.7 x 0.8 mm
Wafer Size:             6-inch
Number of Resonators:   5
Electrode Material:     Pt/Al
Passivation:            SiO2
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open COMSOL Multiphysics 6.2 and load the Multiplexer Module template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: 36° YX LiTaO3 with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 1822.7 MHz, BW 261.6 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 2.0 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (WLP (Wafer Level Package)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (6-inch, 36° YX LiTaO3).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Rohde & Schwarz FSW Signal Analyzer.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 5468 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 2.0 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 22.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 392 MHz offset >= 33.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 7 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 4.2 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +33 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 500 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 85%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2024-10-31
Devices Tested:         10
Insertion Loss (meas):  1.69 dB
Return Loss (meas):     24.5 dB
Rejection (meas):       35.6 dB
Isolation (meas):       24.9 dB
Q Factor (meas):        7393
Group Delay Variation:  5.8 ns
Power Handling:         +28 dBm
Die Yield:              99.0%

Result Classification:  FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Multiplexer Module design demonstrated below-target performance for WiFi 5 GHz.
b) Insertion loss met target specification.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Temperature stability was within specification across full range.
e) No delamination observed after 1000-cycle thermal shock test.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Optimize resonator geometry to reduce insertion loss by ~0.3 dB.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Escalate to advanced materials team for alternative piezoelectric stack.
